methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier is a Seed-stage transportation company that has raised $7.2M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of three private transportation firms (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride); no public comparables exist in this narrow frontier-tech segment.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum statistical thresholds, peer-median valuation was not applicable. Instead, stage-progression methodology provides the primary signal. Using total capital raised ($7.2M) as a valuation proxy and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $18M. This approach assumes Navier's next financing will reflect typical capital efficiency and investor confidence patterns for the stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $21M, with $18M as the median point. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct-stage peer data to validate the 2.5x multiplier in transportation specifically, and limited visibility into Navier's capital efficiency relative to the three identified comparables. The valuation is therefore sensitive to actual Series A market conditions and investor appetite for frontier transportation technologies at the time of next fundraising.
